call.sequence_note: A second call, and one that happened by accident. The prospect joined a stale link because of a BST timezone mismatch — "my thing has a BST, so it's still on UK time" — while the scheduled call was for the following day at 9am. The rep opened with "I wasn't expecting you to be honest." A prior closer call had already covered discovery and presented the offer, and the prospect refers to it directly: "obviously from the phone call before, you hopefully have seen that it's something that I'm really interested in" and "everything on the call towards the end of the call kind of fast-tracked." An onboarding call with Trevor had been booked off the back of that call and was cancelled during this one. The prospect had also emailed his timing concern in advance, which the rep had read but not answered.

signals: LOW CONFIDENCE — this is a second call with no discovery content. The assignment leans almost entirely on the rep's read-backs from the prior call and should be superseded by the extraction of that call if it is in the corpus.
Price was never mentioned by either party and the prospect agreed to a deposit within seconds of it being proposed, so cost is not presenting as a barrier.
The obstacle is a plateau rather than damage: "you've been in roughly the same routine for a few years now" and "you said to yourself, it's not acceptable to you", both confirmed by the prospect.

Concerned with doing it properly rather than with whether it works — "I don't want to project to you that I'm going to be on top of it" and "it wouldn't be good for me... to know that the first month of me doing this has been subpar to what I want for myself."
International relocation to New York plus a booked family holiday imply means but nothing about occupation, income, health or starting point was established on this call.

goals.text: Break out of a routine he has been stuck in for several years and finds unacceptable
Make the move to New York a genuine fresh start rather than another reset
Do the programme properly and at full effort rather than at half capacity

pains.text: Lost all momentum around May when work got busy and had to rebuild from scratch
Has been in the same routine for a few years and considers that unacceptable
July is fragmented by a booked family holiday and an international move to New York — travel, apartment moves and time-zone disruption
Fears starting badly and letting himself down — "it doesn't make me feel good either because I feel like I'm failing on myself because I haven't been able to keep up"

objections.raw_quote: I've got a family holiday booked, and I'm already planning to move back to New York in July. So I know it's going to be, it won't be showing my full commitment. I just don't think there's any point in, in doing it.
objections.rep_response: Ran the OD play thoroughly and well. Acknowledged first without conceding ("I hear you on being busy, like moving to US, holidays, all of that. And I'm not dismissing it"), then used the prospect's own history against the objection — "you've been busy before, too. To May, this year, you dropped everything because work got crazy, and you lost momentum, and you had to rebuild it from scratch" — then asked the core question, "when life has ever actually slowed down enough to feel like it's a perfect time to start?", then painted the compounding-delay picture of August becoming September and October with nothing changed, then reframed the fresh start ("why would you start the fresh start in August when you can start now?") and repositioned the product as built for exactly this ("He's there for the guys who are on the move, who has busy lives"). The prospect conceded every premise and held his position anyway.

objections.raw_quote: if Trevor had given me four workouts in the week and then, you know, I do two because I've been running around, then it's like, it doesn't make me feel good either because I feel like I'm failing on myself because I haven't been able to keep up.
objections.rep_response: Handled practically and honestly rather than by the script. He reset the expectation — "One month is not for getting you significant results... when you're fixing something that's been for years, you cannot fix it in one month" — and then reduced the perceived load: "the first month is basically just dialing in all the movements, so probably it won't be even the four workouts. Maybe it's going to be two, like everything is designed that has to fit you." He backed it with his own experience of being gassed and sore early on. The prospect acknowledged it but was not moved off the August preference.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No price figure was restated on this call; the six-month term was referenced repeatedly but the $6,000 was not. What was structured live is a new instrument: a $100 refundable deposit to hold a start slot at the end of July. "to keep that spot, let's just do, like, a small deposit, $100. So he has the, like, in calendar, okay, there's going to be the guy coming in at the end of July." The rep stated it was "totally refundable" and that a later start would carry no penalty: "If you would say, at the end of July, look, something happened. Let's start mid-August. That's fine." He also stated a gating policy: "I cannot get you on a call with Trevor until the full payment is made." A payment link for the deposit was sent by email during the call; the prospect said he had not yet moved funds and would action it on receipt.

evidence: No payment was taken. The prospect said "I haven't had a chance to do one of that. Give me... Send it... Send me the link", and the deposit link was sent by email during the call with no confirmation of payment before it ended.

The purchase itself remains undecided and was explicitly deferred: the rep booked Monday 27 July at 10am UK time and described its purpose as "just for us, taking care of the payment and then getting with Trevor."
The Trevor onboarding call that existed going into this call was cancelled: "So I need to tell him, like, look, okay, we need to cancel this."

The close rule was considered and not applied. The prospect verbally agreed to a $100 refundable placeholder and a payment link was sent — but what he agreed to move forward on was a fully refundable hold, not the $6,000 programme, and the rep himself scheduled the payment for four weeks later. Treating a refundable deposit as a close would put an undecided deal into a close-rate numerator.

Counter-evidence for a warmer read: intent is high and consistent. He confirmed "it's something that I'm really interested in", agreed to the deposit without hesitation ("Yeah, yeah"), agreed the rep's arguments were valid throughout ("I do agree", "I'm not saying your points are invalid"), and proactively emailed ahead of the call rather than going quiet.

Counter-evidence for a colder read: he is relocating internationally between now and the agreed start date, the agreed start is itself already a slip from the original plan, and the rep pre-authorised a further slip to mid-August at no cost.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to pay a $100 refundable deposit via a link sent by email. Call booked for Monday 27 July at 10am UK time to take full payment and then hand over to Trevor. The previously scheduled Trevor onboarding call was cancelled.

notable.note: The best-executed objection handling in the batch and the most questionable commercial device in it, in the same fourteen minutes. The OD play ran close to complete — the prospect's own May collapse used as evidence, the perfect-time question, the compounding-delay picture, the fresh-start reframe — and the prospect agreed with every premise and still did not move. The rep then conceded the August start and invented a $100 refundable deposit to hold it, justifying it as something Trevor would require while stating in the same breath that he had not yet spoken to Trevor about it: "now I need to talk to him... But he's gonna tell me, okay, so get him, like, a commitment." He also stated a gating policy — "I cannot get you on a call with Trevor until the full payment is made" — while cancelling a Trevor call that had been booked without payment. Note too that this call only happened because of a timezone error on a stale invite, and that the prospect's emailed concern had been read and left unanswered.

Clear examples: the long "I've seen it happen with guys who delay the start" passage at 00:04:00 is labelled as the rep but opens mid-sentence from the prospect's turn; "Well, everything always could be better, but that makes no sense" at 00:09:04 is the rep inside the prospect's block; "No, the thing is, like, I cannot get you on a call with Trevor until the full payment is made" at 00:10:40 sits under the prospect's label and is unambiguously the rep; "Send that to me as soon as possible and I'll get it done in the next couple of months" at 00:12:07 is the prospect and "months" is almost certainly an ASR error for minutes. Because the deposit and payment-gating statements both fall inside inverted blocks, their attribution was established from sense rather than labels; both readings are unambiguous.
